decision: The cache prototype clears the original copper-neck assertion in this run, but still fails the original full-board worker-time gate. No runtime admission.

copper_neck.scope: The passing assertion bounds check time only. Complete process time also includes board parsing and copper-layer construction and must not be reported as the check duration.

runner_correction: The first native runner searched stdout for progress emitted to stderr after the full-board test had already finished. The followup validates both retained streams and runs only the omitted copper-neck test; the full-board failure was not overwritten or rerun.
comparison_limits: The current native main checkpoint failed at 202.370870026 worker seconds and 98.539989332 copper-neck check seconds in a full-library run. Those numbers and this isolated candidate process are not a fixed matched application experiment. Finding counts agree, but counts do not establish exact report-byte identity. No causal application-speedup, complete consumer-suite or full-plan claim is made.
remaining: The first-query and opaque-control scalar costs and added retained memory remain unresolved tradeoffs. Full board admission still requires the original 120-second gate, broader consumer correctness, cache-frontier checks and complete report replay.
next_step: Diagnose cache-assisted projection success, fallback frequency and remaining native layer-sanity callers on a separately instrumented source snapshot before choosing another runtime change. Preserve the current candidate and all original fixtures and limits.
